data.source_title: 2022 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway on the Evaluation and Disposition of Acute Chest Pain in the Emergency Department
data.locator: Sections 5.2.1 (Initial ECG Interpretation), 5.3 (hs-cTn Assays), and pathway figures; key points 1–3
data.source_setting: U.S. emergency department; adult acute chest-pain evaluation, especially possible ACS; requires validated high-sensitivity troponin assay pathways.
value: Obtain and interpret an ECG within 10 minutes of ED arrival; review prehospital ECG when available.
Patients with ischemic ECG findings follow acute STEMI/NSTE-ACS guidance; nonischemic ECG patients may enter an accelerated clinical decision pathway.
Use assay-specific high-sensitivity troponin testing and serial change within a validated rapid pathway to guide rule-out, observation/testing, or high-risk disposition.
data.source_evidence_basis: The consensus pathway states ECG should be obtained/interpreted within 10 minutes, identifies ischemic ECG as prompting acute ACS guideline management, and describes hs-cTn rapid pathways for patients with nonischemic ECGs. The source specifically cautions these pathways are not suitable for older-generation assays.
data.limitations: Clinical pathway, not a complete differential for all chest pain. Depends on local validated assay-specific thresholds and timing; definite ACS management is outside this document’s scope.
data.inferred_scenario_use: A synthetic ED case may expose arrival, ECG interpretation, troponin collection/result review, risk-pathway branch, and disposition as separate decisions; do not simulate numeric assay thresholds without local validated protocol and clinician review.
data.applicability: Adult ED patients with acute chest pain and possible ACS; not an automatic diagnosis or treatment rule.
data.source_period: 2022 consensus pathway (publication date 2022-10-11); no cohort period applies.
data.source_n: Not applicable; guideline/pathway, not a patient cohort
data.role_assignment_basis: Role participants are proposed scenario assignments inferred from the pathway setting for simulation design; the cited source does not enumerate this exact role list.
